claim_text: Three named-but-undocketed defendants in this corpus, previously listed only as 'charged' with no case_docket recorded, pleaded guilty per a Hiiraan Online tracker: Bekam Addissu Merdassa (co-ran the shell company Youth Inventors Lab) pleaded guilty on October 13 to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, admitting the company never served a meal but collected $3 million by claiming 1.3 million meals served between December 2020 and June 2021; Hadith Yusuf Ahmed (previously monitored Feeding Our Future food sites for enrollment compliance) pleaded guilty on October 13 to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, admitting he accepted $1 million in kickbacks from food sites and started a shell company, Southwest Metro Youth, that received $1.1 million by falsely claiming to feed 2,000 children a day; Hanna Marekegn (owned Brava Cafe, a Minneapolis restaurant -- a distinct business from the Rochester-based Brava Restaurant & Cafe LLC tied to the Jama family in case 22-CR-225) pleaded guilty on October 13 to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, admitting Brava Cafe received $7.1 million by claiming to serve more than two million meals between September 2020 and January 2022, and that she paid more than $150,000 in bribes to Feeding Our Future employees to enroll her restaurant.

qualifiers: No primary court record has been captured for any of these three defendants; all dispositions rest on a single secondary journalism source.

The plea date given ('October 13') states no year in the retrieved source text; given the article's framing that pleas began trickling in three weeks after the September 2022 charges, this could plausibly be October 2022 or a later October, but this corpus does not assert a specific year without further confirmation.
None of the three defendants has a case_docket recorded in this corpus; this claim does not attempt to assign one.

'Brava Cafe' (Minneapolis, Hanna Marekegn) is a distinct business from 'Brava Restaurant & Cafe LLC' (Rochester, the Jama family, case 22-CR-225); the similarity in name is coincidental and should not be conflated.

The source separately references a co-defendant, Yusuf Ali, who worked with Youth Inventors Lab and was supplied by S&S Catering; this is not confirmed to be the same person as fof-d-030 (Yusuf Bashir Ali) and is not resolved by this claim.
